facts.description: The source of its facts and of the resets they list.

presenter.description: What presents its key, for a provider whose credential is a key.

description:
What a provider's managers chose for each element, as the column `providers.sources` keeps it. An element
left out has its default source: `{}` is what every provider had before sources could be chosen.
title: ProviderSources

name.description: The built-in source or the program, by name.

address.description:
The address, with how it is authorized and whether the provider's key may be sent to it. The
authorization itself is the provider secret `source:<element>:authorization`.

config.description: What the provider's managers gave for the source's fields that are no secrets.

secrets.description:
The source's secret fields that have a value, by name; each value is the provider secret
`source:<element>:field:<name>`.

descriptor.description: What the source said it is, the last time it was asked.

described_at.description:
When it was last asked what it is: an address is asked again a day later, and after an answer in
another shape or one that it does not implement.

last_error.description: The last error of the source, until a read succeeds.

SourceChoice.description:
What a provider's managers chose for one element, as `providers.sources` keeps it: the choice, with the
names of the secret fields that have a value instead of their values, the descriptor learned from the
source, and its last error.

oneOf.description:
What follows from the provider's credential and endpoints ([`default_source`]): its harness for a
sign-in, a vendor's reads of a key at its hosts, each endpoint's list of models, else nothing.
A built-in source, by `name` ([`builtin`]).
A program registered on the machine that keeps the credential, by `name`.
An address, reached from the machine that keeps the credential.

Nothing: no facts are read beside what the keeper reports, no models are listed (they are added by
name), no key is presented but by its own rule.

url.description: The address requests are posted to.

auth.description: How requests to it are authorized.

send_credential.description:
Whether the provider's key is sent to it, as `params.credential.key`: only where its managers turned
that on for this address, and only for a key.

SourceAddress.description:
An address a source is reached at, with how it is authorized and whether the provider's key may be sent
to it. The authorization itself is a provider secret, never part of it.

oneOf.description: It is not.
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
The token as the value of the header named in `header`.

AddressAuth.description: How a request to an address is authorized: as an endpoint's key is presented.

name.description: Its name: one of a kind among the programs of a machine, and among the built-in sources.

summary.description: What it is, in one sentence.

contract.description: The version of this contract it speaks.

facts.description: What it tells of the facts; `null` when it implements no facts.

fields.description:
What it asks of a provider's managers. A secret field is kept as the provider secret
`source:<element>:field:<name>`, written once and never shown again.

SourceDescriptor.description:
What a source declares: what it is, which of the interfaces it implements, and what it asks of a
provider's managers.

reports.description:
The members it can tell. A member it does not list is unsupported until it tells it; a name this
contract does not know is left out.

spends_resets.description: Whether it spends the resets it lists in `available_resets` (`resets.spend`).

credential.description: Whether it wants the provider's key to read.

min_interval_secs.description: The least time between two of its reads, in seconds, at least 60; `null` leaves it to Orch.

plans.description: The plans it may name in `plan`, by id, with the name to show for each.

SourceDescriptorFacts.description: What a source tells of a provider's facts.

oneOf.description: The plan's id.
The usage windows of the plan.
A limit that has been reached.
Whether the vendor admits ordinary use now.
What is left to be spent.
What has been spent, over periods.
Spending beyond the plan.
Resets that can be spent.
Who the credential belongs to.
How the credential was given and when it lapses.
Whether this read authenticated with the provider's credential.

FactMember.description:
A member of [`ProviderFacts`] that a source can tell, as its descriptor lists it and `facts_state`
answers it.

oneOf.description: It reads without the key.

It wants the provider's key; it is given only where the provider's credential is a key (and, for an
address, only where the provider's managers turned that on for it).

SourceCredential.description: Whether a source wants the provider's key to read its facts.

SourceDescriptorModels.description:
What a source declares of the models it lists. It has no members yet: that it is there says that the
source implements `models.list`.

SourceDescriptorPresents.description:
What a source declares of the key presentation it makes. It has no members yet: that it is there says
that the source implements `credential.present`.

name.description: The member the answer is given under.

label.description: What the person reads beside it.

required.description: Whether an answer must be given.

default.description: What stands in the form before the person writes.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes an answer may have.

Field.description: One thing a person is asked for.

oneOf.description: One line of text.
One line that is never shown again.
Several lines that are never shown again, such as a key file.
One of the field's choices.
Yes or no.
A calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`.
Names with values.
Names with values that are never shown again.

FieldType.description: What kind of value a field takes.

message.description: The source's sentence: at most 300 characters, every secret the machine holds replaced by `[secret]`.

SourceChoiceLastError.description:
The last error of a source, kept beside its choice and shown where the source is: its facts keep their
values and times, and the provider's status is untouched.

oneOf.description: The method is not implemented.
The source could not tell now: its vendor was silent.
The vendor refused this read.
No answer within the method's deadline.
The program is down or restarting, the address cannot be reached, or it answered HTTP 5xx or 429.
The answer is not in its shape: the message names the first wrong member.
The answer is over its size, or a list over its cap.
An address answered with a redirection, which is never followed.
An address refused the authorization Orch holds for it (HTTP 401 or 403).
The address is not among the upstreams a person's machine allows.
A key could not be presented for a model request.

SourceErrorCode.description: Why a source did not answer as asked. The codes are the same for every binding.
